To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have developed a new somewhat homomorphic cryptosytem, which can be used to construct an efficient and secure protocol for multiparty computation.
we can: • Compute a secure 64bit multiplication with three players in 0.1 s (online phase).

(i) our protocol can securely compute any arithmetic circuit with 3 players in a constant number of rounds, and (ii) the computational cost of the preprocessing is O(n/s) where s is a system parameter that is independent of the number of players n and the size of the circuit to be computed.
In summary, our research is concerned with
multiparty computation over large fields and we show that the computational complexity of the preprocessing phase is essentially the same as that of the actual computation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we have the best known multiparty computation protocol for 3 players.

our scheme is the first to combine the following features: (1) it allows for secure computation of arithmetic circuits, (2) it is secure against an active and malicious adversary corrupting up t players for any t < n, (3) the online phase is both communication and computational efficient, and (4) the online phase does not require any public-key operations.
we provide a practical and efficient multiparty computation protocol for large fields.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the preprocessing phase has a total computational (and bandwidth) complexity of O(n2s) and O(n2s), respectively, while the online phase has a total complexity of O(n) in both.
we provide the first practical multiparty computation protocol for 3 players that is secure against an active (byzantine) adversary.
our protocol is the fastest multiparty protocol secure against an adaptive adversary, and the first that is secure against an active (malicious) adversary in large fields.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of somewhat homomorphic encryption can be very efficient in the context of multiparty computation.
we can perform secure computation of circuits in large fields with a preprocessing phase that does not depend on the function to be evaluated.
secure multiparty computation can be made very efficient, even for large fields, if the preprocessing is not required to be secure.
